# Implementation Plans

<!-- awf:edit intro: default; create .awf/parts/plans-readme/intro.md to override -->
A plan is the change-specific execution record for a complex change: observable outcomes, authority links, material boundaries, ordering dependencies, focused evidence, and confinement where ambiguity or helpers require it. For hand-authored production-code work, its Architecture summary must preserve the proportionate outline that received explicit user approval so an explicit request to execute the named plan can reuse that evidence. Workflow skills and agents own generic staging, gates, clean trees, commits, review routing, recovery, checkpoints, and model selection. The design rationale lives in the linked ADR (when one exists); a plan links to it structurally through `adrs:` rather than restating it. If planning discovers a new durable choice that remains meaningful after implementation, return to ADR authoring instead of hiding that choice in a task.

<!-- awf:edit naming: default; create .awf/parts/plans-readme/naming.md to override -->
## Naming & location

Plans live in `docs/plans/` and follow this pattern:

```
YYYY-MM-DD-kebab-topic.md
```

where the date is the day the plan is written (ISO-8601). Example:
`2026-01-15-extract-refs-package.md`.

<!-- awf:edit structure: default; create .awf/parts/plans-readme/structure.md to override -->
## What a plan contains

- Frontmatter starts with `format: plan-v2`, then `date`, `adrs: []` (numbers or retained pending slugs), and the two-state `status`. Marker-absent historical plans retain legacy checks and plan-v1 retains its compatibility grammar and projection.
- A nonempty `# Plan: <Title>`, `## Goal`, and `## Architecture summary` precede one or more sequential `## Phase P: <title>` sections. File structure and Verification are not plan-v2 sections.
- Each phase independently declares exactly one execution mode: `inline` or `subagent-driven`, may directly follow it with nonempty JSON `Advances` then `Completes` arrays of unique `dod:` slugs, contains sequential `### Task P.T: <title>` headings, and ends with one final `### Phase close` carrying exactly one non-ignored `commit` fence. A phase is one independently green coherent implementation transaction, and heading-identified tasks are ordered steps rather than completion, dispatch, review, checkpoint, or commit boundaries. A subagent-driven phase declares its change-specific dependencies; its owner owns generic baseline protocol.
- Tasks state change-specific observable outcomes, relevant authority links, material boundaries, ordering dependencies, focused evidence, and explicit confinement where ambiguity or helpers require it. `Latitude`, `Kind: batch`, `Representative`, and `Edge` are optional aids; historical grammar remains valid. `TBD`, `implement later`, outcome-only summaries, and hidden design choices are placeholders, never pseudocode; every task remains executable by an agent with no prior conversation context.
- Write applicable fields contiguously and directly beneath the task declaration and before prose. The vocabulary is `Kind: spike`, `Kind: batch`, `Latitude: exact`, `Question:`, `Applying:`, `Context:`, `Paths:`, `Representative:`, `Edge:`, and `Post-check:`. `Applying:` and `Context:` carry nonempty JSON string arrays and are omitted rather than written as `[]`; their entries are unique `<adr-identity>:<decision-slug-or-#N>` references; Applying targets plan-level `adrs:` commitments and Context is frozen history or design input. `Paths:` is a JSON array of repository-relative literal, `glob:`, or `pathspec:` strings.
- A `Kind: spike` task is question-only, carries `Question:`, has no implementation body, records its answer in Notes, cannot own a phase, and sequences dependent work into a later phase. A `Kind: batch` task carries `Paths:` and deterministic `Post-check:`; `Representative:` and `Edge:` are optional aids. `Paths:` is required whenever affected scope is ambiguous, including an ambiguous non-batch task; every batch is necessarily ambiguous. `Post-check:` is required for every batch and whenever `Paths:` contains a `glob:` or `pathspec:` entry. Conditional and optional tasks are forbidden.
- Any helper partition exhaustively assigns every affected site to the parent or exactly one helper, keeps helper subsets path-disjoint, shared files parent-owned, and mutating commands confined to the assigned subset. Helpers are sequential and commit-disabled. Commit-capable owners may resolve authority-determined local symbols, helper structure, test arrangement, and necessary omitted paths inside approved boundaries; helpers remain confined. Each Phase close names one closing commit; generic protocol belongs to execution workflow owners.
- Required `## Definition of done` contains one or more observable whole-plan bullets beginning with unique `` `dod: <slug>` `` markers. Any number of phases may each advance an outcome, but at most one phase may complete it; Proposed plans emit non-failing notes for omitted Applying assignments, unassigned outcomes, and advanced-only outcomes missing a completion owner, while hard structural and reference failures always block. Optional `## Notes` records deviations, spike answers, follow-ups, and findings.

Inline owners immediately correct stale instructions and record reasoned deviations in Notes. Delegated owners may report rather than edit; the parent supplies that report to phase review and reconciles it with findings in one focused post-review settlement commit before checkpointing or later execution. The implementation phase owner performs any focused generated-prose meaning review and records inspected output boundaries and result; reviewers inspect the requirement and evidence.

A plan stays mutable as `status: Proposed` through review and implementation and freezes at `status: Implemented` only in the deferred terminal transaction after assurance settles or is explicitly skipped. `effort-workflow` owns effort-backed closure; the effort-free execution parent owns it otherwise. Plans remain as the historical execution record.
